feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/content/platform roles. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through specific platforms, scale, and scope: Drupal migration, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, analytics stack, studio buildout.  
- Professional, readable writing with a solid executive summary and relevant mix of strategy, technical, and communications expertise.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: e.g., engagement growth, email performance, traffic improvements, production savings, adoption rates, or team/process efficiencies.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “French (A2/learning)” is more stylistically consistent than “A2/Learning.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy leadership, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Reduce the long channel list; “multi-channel” or “cross-channel” already covers web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, CMS and platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that enable effective digital operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also reappear in Topline Skills and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-impact phrasing: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” or “Integrated web, email & social strategy.”
- Combine overlapping workflow items: “Editorial workflow design” + “Workflow & systems architecture” could become “Content operations, workflow & systems design.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Content operations, workflow & systems design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, stakeholder coordination, advocacy messaging, and multimedia.
- “Web & CMS administration” may undersell stronger technical/platform leadership shown in experience.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting-level outcomes, transformation work, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “build and refine,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Streamlined cross-channel workflows,” “launched modular campaign experiences,” “improved governance and usability.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Lead enterprise web and content-operations improvements across Drupal, analytics, and cross-channel communications workflows.
- Built modular campaign microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits for member engagement.
- Provide front-end/CMS implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Shaped an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite work duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for projects.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also overlap with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize advisory/consulting scope here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest web metrics into one bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes sharper where possible: add budget size, team size, % gains in reporting speed, production volume, engagement, or cost savings from the in-house studio.
- Tighten channel language: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; emphasize strategic capacity-building here, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo role above and the earlier digital media role below. Tighten it around operational ownership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Strengthen ops language: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.” Add metrics if possible: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this one as scaling/operationalizing the series.
- “digital publishing workflows” and cross-team planning overlap with the 2022–2024 governance bullet; keep this entry more execution-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance  
- Editorial operations for complex publishing teams  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector advocacy storytelling  
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with your recent roles.
- If space allows, make one phrase more outcome-oriented, e.g., “Governance for high-volume, multi-publisher web operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also repeated in Core Competencies; “storytelling” or “communications” would add variety.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too broad and repeats detail already covered in Technical + IT. For a topline skills line, tighten it around the most relevant, recent strengths and group tools into clearer capability buckets.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the list with: Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint & Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization since recent roles and projects center on Drupal platform rebuilds and web improvement.
- Combine coding tools into one phrase rather than listing each separately; this reads more senior and concise.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale language indirectly via adjacent experience, not here (e.g., 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies; keep it here only if you shorten/remove the similar phrase there.
- Most items overlap with Technical + IT; avoid turning this section into a second software inventory.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic list. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic so it reinforces seniority rather than duplicating the Director role bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Group tools and methods: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery” + “KPI framework design, executive dashboards, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Tighten phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI & BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards & reporting • SEO, UX and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with the Director of Digital Media bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure; keep the skills line broad and capability-focused, not achievement-focused.
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with work experience that already proves video/studio/event capability. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent strengths and use sharper, more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, outcome-oriented language: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio system operation.”
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio operations • Virtual event production”
- If these skills were central in the 2022–2024 director role, prioritize the capabilities tied to building the in-house studio and running recurring advocacy/event programming.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale/context instead of more tools, e.g., “recurring advocacy programming” or “in-house studio production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” is partially redundant; combine into one phrase.
- This item overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies, so keep this version more specific and technical.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is clearly the most relevant/recent platform in the experience section, this item should emphasize proficiency level or platform context rather than repeat a generic list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light qualifiers: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented via label change: **CMS Platforms: Drupal (10,000+ page migration; modular microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep “GitHub Pages” only if you’ve used it professionally; otherwise replace with a more substantive platform or remove for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry listing the same platforms; consider trimming one or using this section for tools not named elsewhere.
- “CMS modernization” already appears in Topline Skills, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you remove it there.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/basic items unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability, e.g. “Front-End & Technical Implementation.”
- Reorder by relevance/recency and group tools by use case: “API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • JavaScript • HTML/CSS • jQuery”
- Consider replacing “HTML5” and “CSS3” with “HTML/CSS” for concision; keep jQuery only if still used in current/target roles.
- If space allows, add scope/outcome language tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g. “API integrations, lightweight edge scripting, deployment automation, and tag management for Drupal-based public web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- GitHub Actions and Cloudflare Workers are useful differentiators—keep those over more basic terms if you need to cut.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Tighten and group by function: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- If space allows, add light context to show application, e.g. “Used to build editorial planning, approvals, intake, and cross-team coordination workflows.”
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools first; if Airtable, Power Automate, and Jira are most relevant to current work, lead with those and consider dropping one weaker PM tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and automation are already mentioned in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same positioning unless this section is purely for tool names.
- Listing Jira, Asana, Basecamp, and Trello together may feel redundant; keep only the platforms actually used recently or at depth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it’s too bare and misses the scale of your recent email leadership. Tie these tools to campaign, newsletter, or member-engagement use so the item feels more relevant and senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** _(campaign automation, newsletter distribution, member engagement)_
- If space allows, make it stronger with context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — used for newsletter operations, campaign journeys, and audience/member communications**
- Keep platform names only if these are tools you used meaningfully in recent roles; otherwise remove the least relevant one.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters; avoid repeating “reaching tens of thousands” here.
- “Engagement” may partially duplicate “Multi-channel communication” and “Workflow & systems architecture” elsewhere, so keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video series, cross-channel publishing.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.
- Tighten to one sentence or two concise bullets, e.g.: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia workflows. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on building capacity and hands-on production.
- Avoid repeating website/email/social leadership language already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/project coordination plus the “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and first-of-its-kind work: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams, translating findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add outcomes: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a more concise final version: “Coordinated innovation and research projects for program and policy teams; developed supporting digital and multimedia content. Launched NACo’s first podcast, managing planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on innovation/research support and the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating generic “supporting organizational programs and policy work” language used elsewhere without a concrete result.
